subject.title: Feature: Pre-compaction agent notification, structured handoff window, and deferral mechanism

question: Should OpenClaw add a new core compaction lifecycle contract for configurable pre-threshold warnings, structured handoff, and bounded defer, or keep the current hooks/checkpoints/memoryFlush model?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but the missing behavior adds public config/tool/protocol surface and changes authority/state continuity at a compaction boundary, which needs maintainer product and security intent.

options.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
options.body: Define warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint fields, deferral governance, defaults, security limits, docs, and tests before implementation.

options.title: Keep Current Primitives
options.body: Document existing hooks, notifier, memoryFlush, and checkpoint branch/restore as the supported extension points and narrow or close this feature direction later.

options.title: Split Into Smaller Decisions
options.body: Track pre-threshold warning, handoff checkpoint schema, and bounded deferral as separate approved design items to reduce surface risk.

recommendation.title: Design Core Lifecycle Contract
recommendation.body: Define warning thresholds, handoff checkpoint fields, deferral governance, defaults, security limits, docs, and tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest available history signal for compaction/memoryFlush design and the remaining blocker is product/security direction.
